topics.label: Lecture opening and framing
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer welcomes students, acknowledges the challenging nature of the topic, and frames the scope of the lecture.

topics.label: Foundations and central role of C3 in complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the basic architecture, naming conventions, and core C3 reaction underlying the complement cascade.

topics.label: Pathogen recognition and activation pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the three pathways responsible for recognizing pathogens and driving complement activation to its trigger threshold.

topics.label: Complement effector mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how activated complement executes pathogen destruction and clearance through downstream effector actions.

topics.label: Regulation of complement and host protection
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic addresses how regulatory proteins protect healthy host tissues by controlling and shutting down complement activation.

topics.label: Clinical complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores the diverse clinical presentations and disease vulnerabilities caused by deficiencies in specific complement proteins.

topics.label: Microbial evasion of complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines the strategies pathogens use to avoid complement destruction and their practical applications in biotechnology.

topics.label: Lecture closing and upcoming topics
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session and provides a preview of the upcoming lecture series.
